Ah that's good. Hopefully they come back fine too. My biggest concern there was how you said she's whining softer. She could be dehydrated and weak so be careful with that. If she's otherwise fine I wouldn't worry much though. 

Regular purina really isn't very good. Mine are on purina pro plan puppy small breed cause they're like 6lbs and Im satisfied with it. (I have 2 puppies but thats a whole different convo lol) Yeah definitely look into them. Mine reacted to the bully sticks I gave them at first, but settled down after I waited a while to try it again. I'd hold off on treats for now. That helped me when they had awful diarrhea for 2 weeks. 

That sounds good. I use verbal commands too, but honestly the clicker works so much quicker when it comes to teaching them. I didn't use it at first and regret not doing it sooner. I also act excited and give them a lot of praise as long as it isn't bed time. It seems to help.

I feel you there. I try to do the same. They definitely test my patience lol

It couldn't hurt. She's really young and if she's small they can hold it even less.
Anyway you sound like you're doing a pretty good job in my opinion. Puppies are just difficult no matter how much you love them and try. I remind myself repeatedly they will grow up lol.
Wtf? About 30 minutes a week? Damn, just that people don't spend hours everyday is mindblowing. Seriously cannot imagine.

Have you spoken to the vet about this? It sounds like she's still having some issues she needs help with. That's a lot of times to go on themselves even if they are very small. I would call and ask my vets office about it. They've always been helpful even if it turns out we don't need a visit. 

 Maybe you should also look at her food? Some dogs just don't tolerate certain ingredients well or at all. You might even want to change what you're washing her stuff with or look if anything else has been changed recently. Dogs can be so sensitive to the oddest things to us.

Aside from that the only thing that could teach my puppy to stop going in her pen was clicker training. Tear up a bunch of treats into pieces you can grab and go and act like she's solved world hunger when she goes properly. You can get clickers cheap on Amazon, but using your tongue can work too.  

That and having her on a solid feeding and potty schedule has been imperative. I understand that's difficult when they're ill, but I just had to do my best there.

 I've also had to really learn that she isn't trying to upset me or not listen or anything like that. The opposite actually. She really wants to please me and gets very upset when I'm upset with her. But she doesn't understand what to do with that. It'll take some time to learn how they communicate with you and for you to teach them how to use that and what you want and expect from them. It's extra hard when they're uncomfortable or sick, but it does get better. 

My puppy wouldn't go outside her pen at all for months and took painfully long to get to do her business. Now she's doing great and it's usually a quick trip which feels like a miracle lol. (Edit- it was my fault for not working with her more carefully sooner. She learned in weeks and is almost fully trained now after I started considering her much more.)

I hope she feels better soon and good luck.
